description: Phase 8 family 24: the Plague Lords Xatma, K'zrath and Vesh (Tombs of Terror chapter 1-3 final bosses; family 01's F01.json keeps Icarax, chapter 4, family 24's own row), phased bosses with persistent damage, and Tekahn, the Tombs finale fought with the explorers' hero relay. Boss deck lists are transcribed from hearthstone.wiki.gg boss pages (read 2026-11-14), by card name; Tekahn's relay decks are the client's finale decks, by card id.
method: The wiki's raw wikitext (?action=raw) was read for each page and the Normal deck tables transcribed in table order, rowspan-aware, up to the "Extra cards in 33-deck" rows; a boss-only or ambiguous card carries its id. Written by verify/tools/gen/p8f24/make_f24.py; tools/dungeon-run-catalog (step 'encounters') resolves and checks every card.

adaptations.note: The three phases are forms of one row with one falling Health total (300; phase 2 at 200 or less, phase 3 at 100 or less, the remaining Health kept); a lost fight's damage is banked per encounter at profile scope (DungeonRunProfile.BossDamage, as family 01's Icarax), because a lost fight ends the run; each ULDA_115 cast in the run's other fights banks its 10 plus its Spell Damage (DungeonRunState.PlagueLordDamage), and a cast inside the fight deals it to the lord at once.

A phase change replaces the deck with the phase's Normal list and draws 3 cards from it (the wiki: "draws three extra cards before his main deck"); the wiki's extra cards of the 33-card phase decks are not added, and a fight that starts in phase 2 or 3 (banked damage) starts with that phase's deck and no extra cards, as the wiki says.
The wiki marks some phase powers "Auto-cast"; here every clickable power is the boss AI's choice (family 01's precedent for Elder Brandlemar).

modifierReasons.mod_iron_bosses: the row's Health is its identity (fixedHealth: DungeonRun.BossHealth ignores bossHealthDelta), so Iron Bosses' +5 never reaches the fight; a stamp-4 schedule neutralises the modifier for this fight only (DungeonRun.NeutraliseKnobs; its extra treasure after a major is kept), a released one bans it for the act
modifierReasons.mod_open_road: the row's Health is its identity (fixedHealth), so Open Road's +3 boss Health never reaches the fight and only its extra opening card would; a stamp-4 schedule neutralises the modifier for this fight only (no extra card), a released one bans it for the act

adaptations.note: Tekahn keeps one hero (ULDA_BOSS_67h, 300 Health) through three phases; the wiki names no phase thresholds, so they are the Plague Lords' (phase 2 at 200 or less, phase 3 at 100 or less): power-only forms that replace the deck with the phase's Normal list (40 cards each) and draw no extra card (the wiki states none). Tekahn keeps no damage between attempts (the wiki), so the row has no persistentDamage.

The finale's hero relay (schedule finale heroRelay): the run's own hero fights first, then the four explorers less the run's own (skipFor), each at 50 Health with one of its three client finale decks (ULDA_<Explorer>_Tekanh_Deck_n) and its hero power n, the entry drawn by the match's game RNG as the explorer enters (EncounterRules.ResolveRelay; the boss's fair view, a clone with its own RNG, cannot know it beforehand). The original lets the player choose the next explorer and its hero power; here they enter in the wiki's order (Elise, Finley, Brann, Reno) and the entering hero draws the model's RelayDraw cards (family 01), not a full hand; collected signature treasures are not shuffled in.

Curse of Flame's enchantment fires at the start of the boss's next turn while the cursed minion is in play, then the curse ends; Soul Pyre deals the Cost paid for the card (the engine's last known Cost in hand).
